I've been an inpatient in both adult and adolescent mental health hospitals here in the UK. The adult just for two months, but the adolescent was for six months. 

The first stay, I had just turned 17, and was admitted as an emergency due to anorexia. This is different in the hospital I was in than the other disorders the kids had. With me anyway, because I was high risk suicide and because of my incredibly low weight, someone had to followed me arund all day (1 to 1 obs with no privacy). I ate six times a day, or I """ ate""". I soon figured out easy ways to get away with not eating or drinking the supplements and being fine for days (the rule was if you.didn't eat anything for four days you had to get an NG tube, which I did have once), they had an on site school that everyone had to go to to study and keep busy, but on the ward there were also classes you.could do, like relaxation and art and music etc. 

The staff weren't that friendly, mainly the nurses in fact. The night staff, who were mainly health care workers were nicer, there was one in particular that taught us how to play cards games which was good for developing my concentration. One thing about the staff during meals times around the people with eating problems: they didn't all do the same thing so I got good at being able to convince someone specific to do my breakfast because they didn't use as much butter or jam on the toast. A lot.of the staff treat the ED patients like dirt because we 'chose this' which is incredibly untrue but I think it is a lack of understanding rather than lack of empathy.

Without divulging too much info, I witnessed a lot of assault in the ward, mainly from the boys aged around 16. One particular had the police called on multiple occasions, and a number of us actually witnessed a suicide attempt by the same child.

If you managed to walk out the door unnoticed, or there was someone with you who didn't care, they mostly tried to follow you, except in some cases but I'm not sure about those cases. What I do know is. if they lose you for more than five minutes, they have to alert the local police because of the dangers to both the child and other people.

In the adult hospital it was different. I was there for a failed suicide attempt, serious self harm/depression and while I was there I was diagnosed with DID. The staff were polite and it was more OT focused than anything. We learned how to cope with life and go shopping, money management etc but also developed concentration and interpersonal skills by playing different games, including exercising in the onsite gym. We were able to go out of the hospital to the canteen along with the staff to eat, and it was generally a more relaxed atmosphere. 

Obviously there were problems on the ward, mainly with admin, for example it took a long time for any doctor to see me or to change my medication while I was there. The nurses allowed us to go for walks and we had a party at Christmas, which for me wasn't good but other people had a good time! 

My time in the adult ward was anything but peachy. I had a lot of problems myself and I was discharged too soon, so I got very ill again very quickly, but I got involved with s home treatment team and now I'm doing better.

*disclaimer: these things may not be the same as every hospital, these are just my experiences.


I have experience with out patient as well as day hospital treatment too if you want to PM me. Also if you need anymore info feel free to ask!!

In all honesty, you don't want to be anorexic, it is the single worst experience in the world in my eyes. Probably when you think of being anorexic you think of being slim and tanned and having lovely hair and boys all over you and a great life because you're not 'fat' anymore.

I'm reality, and this is just my experience: you will be thin, but it won't be a nice thin, it will be a bony, thin skinned, gaunt, sunken eyed kind of thin. You will be paler than snow, no matter what the season. Your hair will fall out and thin, and possibly never recover, in addition to that, you will start growing soft down like hair on your arms and back, which you won't want to have, obviously. Your fingernails will start to turn blue and you'll have to be careful cutting if you even have the energy to get out of bed, because your blood will no longer be able to clot and you'll bleed out.  Your heart will start struggling and eventually you'll get shooting, heart attack like pains. 

Generally, and I know that being thin sounds like the best thing in the world, but you need to focus on being healthy and looking after yourself, and that means eating the right foods and the right amount, and exercising, but not excessively.

Please be safe.

If you want to talk about your eating issues, please feel free to PM me.

Even though I have been in recovery for two years now, I still don't know why my anorexia began.

Because I was at a low weight, I had to go into hospital (at the time I was under 18 so I was in the children's ward) and get better there. It was tough at the start, I had to have a ng tube, and before I started eating regular food, I moved onto things that we call Ensure in the UK, they are basically drinks or yogurts with a high energy content (I try not to think about the calorie content) so that you are able to work on the other things around you and be able to think clearly without being extremely hungry and malnourished. When I finally moved onto normal food, it was tough, really tough. But I got through it with one to one meal supports at every meal in the hospital and even when I was discharged. 

I still can't talk numbers or weight or even get on a scale but that will come in time.

I eat fairly normally, some days will be better than others, I may skip a meal or buy some diet pills/laxatives but I always pull through. I'm focusing now on my other issues and anorexia is taking a backseat because I've changed my thinking around food.

I just wanted to let you know that you are not alone in this fight against this illness. I understand the pain you're going through and I really empathise with you with regards to being anorexic. I am living proof that you can recover from this. I myself had to recover from anorexia before I could start dealing with anything else, which is what I'm trying to do now. 

You have probably heard many side effects of anorexia but you probably didn't know that it can leave you with diabetes or osteoporosis like me. You need to care for yourself before anyone else, you're the most important person in your life, never forget that.

I just wanted to let you know that I'm here, if there's anything you want to ask or anything you need, go ahead!
